title: test-bm configuration
description: Per-bookmarklet test configuration for test-bm.js. Each key is a bookmarklet name, which is the file name in JSFormatted without its .js. A bookmarklet with no entry gets the default safe run: example.com, one run, a settle period, and a pass when it parsed, ran and threw nothing.

$schema.description: Points at this file, so an editor offers completion and validation.

entry.description: What a run does with one bookmarklet.

url.description: The page to open. Defaults to https://example.com/, which is reserved for documentation. A url of the form fixture:<file>.html is a page in test/fixtures/pages, served from https://fixtures.test/ without a network: a real origin, so localStorage, the clipboard and location behave as they do on a site. A hash may follow the file name. A fixture naming a page that is not there is a configuration error. A url of the form $NAME names an environment variable holding the address, for a page whose address does not belong in the repository: the address is read when the entry runs and never written down, every reason and report naming the variable in its place, and an unset variable is a skip rather than a failure.

capture.description: Write a screenshot of the page either side of the bookmarklet, and a video of the whole entry, into test-results/test-bm/<run>/capture/<name>/. Each artifact's path and the offset into the video at which every step started go in the report, so a clip can be cut to the moment the bookmarklet ran. --capture does the same for every entry a run reaches. A failure keeps failure.png whether or not the entry asked to be captured. An entry with auth captures nothing and refuses this, because a signed-in page shows the account and what it holds.

scheduled.description: Include this entry in node test-bm.js --scheduled. Only for pages that load headless with no consent wall and no bot check.

requires.description: The CSS selectors the bookmarklet reads, taken from its source rather than from memory. Each is checked before the bookmarklet runs, and a missing one fails with "site changed: <selector> not found on <url>".

steps.description: What to do on the page, in order. The bookmarklet runs once: at the step that names it, or after load when no step does.

dialogs.description: Answers to alert, confirm and prompt, in the order they appear. A dialog with no answer left is dismissed.

permissions.description: Browser permissions the context grants, such as clipboard-read and clipboard-write. An expect on a clipboard value needs clipboard-read. Firefox has no clipboard permission to grant, its clipboard being open to the page already, so a run there leaves those two out and grants the rest.

skip.description: A reason to list the entry as skipped without running it. A skip never fails a run.
examples: the page serves a consent wall to a headless browser

timeout.description: Milliseconds the whole entry is allowed, after which it fails.

settle.description: Milliseconds to wait after the last step, for anything the bookmarklet started.

auth.description: The sign-in this entry needs, by site name. test-bm.js never signs in itself: it asks the launcher module named by TEST_BM_AUTH_LAUNCHER, an absolute path outside the repository, for a signed-in browser context. Without one the entry is a skip. An entry with auth runs read-only, writes down nothing the page shows, names signedIn, and is never scheduled. Entries that share a sign-in share the name.

network.description: The hosts other than the page's own that the bookmarklet may send a request to, each with the reason. A request the bookmarklet makes to any other host fails the entry, because a bookmarklet sends nothing from the page anywhere else. A site's own API on another host, or a library pinned by its integrity hash, is what belongs here.

host.description: An exact host, or *. and a domain for any of its subdomains.

examples: the file sizes come from GitHub's own REST API

signedIn.description: A selector only the signed-in page has, checked before requires. With auth, a page without it, or one that lands on another origin, is a skip reading "signed out of <site>" rather than a site-changed failure. With drive everyday the driver looks for it first, and a page without it is a skip reading "sign-in wall", since nothing here signs in.

drive.description: Run the entry in the maintainer's everyday browser rather than in one test-bm.js starts, for a site that answers an automated browser with a bot check or a page only the maintainer's own profile shows. test-bm.js never reaches that browser itself: it hands the entry to the module _TEST_BM_EVERYDAY_DRIVER names, an absolute path outside the repository, and keeps only the verdict, the driver's own reason, which input each step sent and how many real runs it made. Without a driver the entry is a skip. An everyday entry is never scheduled, takes no auth, captures nothing, grants no permissions, names no network, opens a site's own https page, answers no prompt, and presses only Tab, Escape, the arrows, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Backspace and Delete.

personal.description: The page shows what the account holds, such as a mailbox, a chat or a watch history, so the entry is kept to selectors, counts and states: no withText, no desktop input, and no expect on text, the clipboard, a stored value, matches or a check. Goes with drive everyday, and names signedIn.

browsers.description: The engines this entry runs in when the run names none with --browser. Without it the entry runs in chromium alone, which is also all --scheduled uses unless an entry asks for more. --browser <engine> runs every entry in that one engine whatever this says. In firefox, every request to another host after the bookmarklet first ran is judged as the bookmarklet's, since firefox does not say which code started it; an entry that counts requests, or has auth, is a skip there. An entry with auth runs in chromium only, and naming another engine here is a configuration error.

step.description: One thing to do. Exactly one of run, bookmarklet, click, hover, fill, press, select, wait, answer, detach, attach, viewport or expect.

bookmarklet.description: Another bookmarklet in JSFormatted, by name, run here first in the same page, the way a reader runs one bookmarklet to set up what the next one reads. Its file is checked as the entry's own is before anything opens, its errors fail the entry, and the requests its code sends are judged as the entry's own. An entry with one names its own run with a run step.

hover.description: A selector to move the pointer over.

button.description: The mouse button a click presses. Defaults to left.

withText.description: With a click or a hover, the first match whose own text is this, matched whole, with runs of white space read as one.

at.description: With a click or a hover, the point to aim at as an offset from the element's centre, in CSS pixels, rather than the centre itself.

via.description: In an entry with drive everyday, how the driver sends a click, hover, fill or press: cdp, events inside the tab, which cannot reach another window, or desktop, the computer's own mouse and keyboard aimed at the one window the page is in. Defaults to cdp. A personal page takes cdp only.

run.description: Run the bookmarklet here, rather than after load. A second run step runs it again, which is how a bookmarklet that turns itself off on the second run is checked. An object with set runs it with variables set first.

set.description: Variables to set before this run, each to a string. The file has to declare each name exactly once, as var <name> = "<string>"; the value replaces that string, written as a string literal, and the file so changed is checked again before any browser starts. Nothing is written back to the file.

fill.description: A selector to type into, with the value beside it or nested in an object.

press.description: A key to press, such as Enter or Control+c. With a selector beside it, the key goes to that element.

select.description: A selector whose text to select, the way a reader drags across it. The range is set inside the element's text node, which is the shape a drag leaves and the shape the bookmarklets that style selected text read.

wait.description: Milliseconds to wait, or a selector to wait for.

detach.description: A selector whose matches are taken off the page and kept, so a state a site produces for a moment - a listing replaced header row and all - lasts long enough to assert against. An attach step puts them back where they came from. The nodes are held in a handle rather than anywhere on the page, so nothing the harness does reaches the page's own scope. A selector matching nothing fails the entry.

attach.description: The name an earlier detach step gave what it took off the page, put back where it came from. A name nothing earlier in the entry detached is a configuration error, and a place that is itself gone by then fails the entry.

viewport.description: The page's size for every step after this one, until another viewport step or the end of the entry, when the entry's own size - 1280x720, or 648x648 for a short - comes back. It is how an expectation that reads geometry, as clear does, is asked at a width a reader's window has and the default does not.

as.description: The name a detach step gives what it took, for an entry that detaches more than one thing. Without it the selector is the name.

selector.description: The element a press goes to.

value.description: The value a fill types, when fill is written as a selector on its own.

text.description: The value a fill types, written the other way round.

expect.description: What should be true. A selector that is visible or hidden, paints its text clear of its neighbours, matches a count, matches as many elements as another selector, or holds some text; or a clipboard value; or where the page is; or where a new tab went; or how many requests the bookmarklet sent to a host; or what the bookmarklet stored; or, in an everyday entry, a check the everyday driver holds.

hidden.description: The first match is not showing.

clear.description: The first match paints its text inside its own border box, and where the text runs past, over nothing that paints text of its own. It is the one expectation that reads geometry: every other one here is satisfied by an element that paints its text straight over the element beside it. Text is measured as glyph runs through Range.getClientRects, and what an overflow lands on is read with elementFromPoint, so a cell a site serves at font-size 0 is clear and the same overflow onto a cell painting its own text is not. A pixel of overlap is a rounding edge rather than text a reader cannot read. The failure names what is covered, by how much, and how much of its width the box holds.

count.description: How many elements the selector matches, exactly.

matches.description: A second selector, whose matches are counted against the first selector's. It is for one thing per row of something the page lists, where the count the page would give changes whenever the page does and the relation does not: a size cell in every file row, say. The failure names both counts.

text.description: Text the first match holds somewhere in it.

clipboard.description: What the clipboard holds, trimmed at both ends: the whole value as a string, or an object for a value no entry could write down in full. selector and attr together are an element's own value, its property of that name or else the attribute, such as the absolute href of a link the bookmarklet added; startsWith, singleLine and nonEmpty say how the value reads. Neither form says in a failure what the clipboard held. Needs clipboard-read in permissions, except in an everyday entry, whose driver reads the clipboard itself.

storage.description: The page's localStorage or sessionStorage, compared with the keys it held before the first bookmarklet ran. Takes newKeys, valueIncludes or both, and no selector. The new keys are removed afterwards unless remove is false, so a run leaves nothing behind. Names and values stay in the page, and a failure gives counts.

newKeys.description: With storage, how many keys are new, exactly.

valueIncludes.description: With storage, text each new key's value holds.
examples: Sample Note: a placeholder for the test

remove.description: With storage, whether the new keys are removed after the check. Defaults to true.

check.description: In an everyday entry, the name of a check the everyday driver holds, for what no selector can say, such as a distance read within a tolerance. Takes no selector.

location.description: Text the page's address holds somewhere in it, for a bookmarklet that navigates. Chromium keeps a text fragment directive out of the address, so a bookmarklet that writes one is read off the page it moved instead.

popup.description: Text the address of a new tab the bookmarklet opened holds somewhere in it, for a bookmarklet that opens a link in a new tab. Waits for the tab, up to the entry's timeout or ten seconds.

requests.description: A host, counted against how many requests the bookmarklet made to it since the last expect that counted the same host, or since the page opened. Takes count for an exact number or atMost for a bound, and no selector. It is what says a directory change costs one request rather than seven, which is a thing no selector on the page can show. A host answered by the entry is counted the same way a host answered by the network is.

atMost.description: A bound on a count of requests rather than an exact number, for a span a site's own re-render can legitimately add one to.

answer.description: A host answered by the entry rather than by the network, so a state only the site's own server produces - the 403 an API gives past its hourly limit, say - is one a run can put the page in. Every request to the host is answered this way until a later step hands it back with pass: true. The answer carries access-control-allow-origin, as a site's own API does, so it reaches the bookmarklet's own code rather than being refused by the browser first. The host is still named in the entry's network with the reason, and its requests are still counted and still judged: a host answered and not named there is a configuration error. The answer is the network's for as long as it stands, so the page's own requests to the host are answered too; what a requests expect counts is still only what the bookmarklet sent.

host.description: An exact host, or *. and a domain for any of its subdomains.

contentType.description: The media type of the body. Defaults to text/plain; charset=utf-8.

body.description: The body to answer with. Defaults to nothing.

pass.description: Hand the host back to the network, for the other half of a state: refusing, then answering again. A host nothing earlier in the entry answers is a configuration error.

accept.description: Accept it rather than dismissing it.

text.description: What to type into a prompt before accepting it.
